new_paragraphs: MyCHEF arranges product launch catering across all of Dubai — from DIFC and Downtown boardrooms to Business Bay showrooms, Dubai Marina rooftops, Palm Jumeirah villas and the exhibition halls of Trade Centre. Wherever your venue, the same vetted-chef standard travels with it. Launches at hotels, galleries, retail stores, co-working spaces and private residences are all routine, and we adapt the setup to each — a compact station kit for an apartment reveal, a full mobile kitchen for a large activation. Because Dubai launches often run late and pivot fast, we staff for flexibility. Pair a product launch with brand activation or a gala dinner , and explore the wider range of event catering . add_block.new_heading: What does product launch catering in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Product launch catering in Dubai includes menu design, a vetted chef, on-site cooking, service staff, setup and cleanup — everything a brand reveal needs, handled by one team. A full brief usually covers passed canapés, one or two live cooking stations, a soft-drink or mocktail bar, and branded finishing touches that echo your product. Because a launch is as much theatre as dining, the food is planned around your run-of-show: bites guests can hold while networking, nothing that needs two hands or a knife. Dietary coverage — halal, vegetarian, vegan, nut-free — is built in from the start, so no guest is left waiting. You get one point of contact, an itemised proposal, and a chef who arrives ready to plate, not to improvise.

add_block.new_heading: Product launch catering for corporate events, brand reveals and parties
new_paragraphs: Corporate product launch catering in Dubai works well when the food matches the stakes of the moment — a car unveiling, a fashion drop, a tech keynote or a retail opening each call for a different rhythm. For a formal corporate reception, we lean on elegant canapés and a plated dessert moment timed to the reveal itself. For a livelier party crowd, live stations and a mocktail bar keep energy high and lines short. It scales cleanly, too: the same kitchen that serves an intimate 20-guest press preview handles a 300-guest activation without dropping standards. We coordinate with your event planner, AV team and venue so food service doesn't clash with the speeches. The goal is plain: guests remember the product, and remember eating well while they discovered it.

add_block.new_heading: What's on a product launch menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A product launch menu in Dubai is built around one-bite, walk-and-talk food: canapés, sliders, sushi, mezze and chef-manned live stations. The menu is designed from a short consultation — we ask about your brand, your guests and any signature colours or flavours you want echoed on the plate. Popular formats include a raw bar, a slider or shawarma station, a grazing table, and a dessert cart that can carry your logo. For a luxury reveal, we add caviar service, aged-cheese towers or a live pasta station. Everything is portioned for standing guests and refreshed in waves, so the last arrival gets the same quality as the first. If you prefer home catering for a smaller founder-and-press gathering in a villa or apartment, the same menus scale down without losing polish.

add_block.new_heading: Launch catering ideas that survive a real room
new_paragraphs: Most catering ideas in Dubai are written for people sitting down. A launch room is the opposite: everyone is standing, holding a drink in one hand and a phone in the other, and half of them are trying to photograph your product. The ideas that work are the ones that respect that. One-bite food, nothing that needs a knife, nothing that drips onto a lanyard. A station that produces smell and sound — a grill, a wok, a robata — because the smell does more marketing across a room than a sign does. Colour rather than logos: matching the dessert and the drinks to your brand palette reads as considered, where a logo printed on every canapé reads as a compromise. And hold something back. A dessert cart or a coffee station that opens twenty minutes after the reveal is the cheapest way to keep a room from emptying the moment the speeches end.

What consistently fails: soup shots, anything served in a bowl needing two hands, a seated course scheduled against a keynote, and one long buffet table that turns into a queue past the very thing you are launching. High end catering in Dubai, at a launch, means fewer items sourced better and more staff per guest — not more trays. A launch is also a hospitality exercise before it is a catering one, and the two are easy to confuse. Press, VIPs, clients and your own team all want different things from the same room: press want to get in, get the shot and get out, VIPs want to be found and looked after, staff want to eat something at some point. That is why service is staffed to the guest list and not to the headcount, and why the floor lead knows who is being watched for.

Where a fired station can stand is a venue question, and it is worth settling before the run-of-show is printed. A robata counter is live charcoal, so it belongs outdoors on a villa's own plot, at ground level on a firm non-combustible base, with a clear standing zone around it — Dubai Municipality's barbecue guidance is explicit that coal is not lit in an enclosed space or indoors. Inside a tower it does not run at all: Emaar's vertical-community rules prohibit barbecues, grills or any cooking equipment of any kind on balconies and terraces regardless of fuel, and no permit unlocks that, because the constraint is the building's extraction and its fire position. For an apartment reveal or an indoor showroom the same skewer menu runs off an electric or induction robata-style counter, or the skewers are charred in the licensed kitchen and finished in front of guests: the chef, the counter and the serve-direct-to-guest rhythm all survive, and the binchotan aroma is the one thing lost. A raw bar has the opposite profile — no flame, no fuel, no extraction requirement — so it runs in a tower, at a villa and on a yacht deck alike, which is why it carries a launch when the fired station cannot. For a rooftop or a desert activation, myCHEF confirms the setup with the building management or the landowner before quoting.

add_block.new_heading: How is branding and timing handled at a launch?
new_paragraphs: Branding and timing are handled by pre-planning every plate against your run-of-show, so the food supports the reveal instead of competing with it. We can brand napkins, station signage, dessert toppers and drink stirrers to your palette, and time the biggest moment — a flambé, a carving, a dessert reveal — to land exactly when your product does. Logistics matter as much as flavour: our team arrives early, sets up discreetly, and needs only power and water for most stations. Timing is mapped to the minute — arrival canapés during registration, stations opening after the keynote, dessert and coffee as the networking winds down. For outdoor or rooftop launches we plan around Dubai's heat with covered stations and chilled service. A private chef leads the floor, so if the schedule shifts, the food shifts with it — no scramble, no cold canapés.

new_paragraphs: Brands do launch during Ramadan in Dubai, and the plan is not the usual plan with the timings nudged. Daytime hospitality is not appropriate while people are fasting, so the event moves to one of two slots. An iftar launch is built backwards from sunset, which is a fixed time you cannot negotiate with: dates and water go out the moment the call comes, the room breaks for prayer within the first twenty minutes, and the real service window opens after that. A run-of-show that puts a keynote at sunset will lose the room entirely. The alternative is a suhoor activation, which runs from roughly 10pm to the pre-dawn hour, suits younger and media-heavy guest lists, and tends to be the livelier of the two. Ramadan catering in Dubai also books out early, and partner kitchens are at their busiest of the year, so a launch in that month wants more notice than one in October. If the event is primarily an iftar, our iftar catering page covers the menu structure in more depth; this page stays with the launch mechanics around it.

add_block.new_heading: How much does product launch catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Product launch catering in Dubai costs from AED 700 per person, with most launches landing between AED 700 and AED 950 per person depending on menu, guest count and service level. Prices scale with the format: a canapé-only reception sits at the lower end, while multi-station or luxury menus with premium seafood rise toward the top. For planning, our launch packages run at AED 1,200, AED 2,400, AED 3,600, AED 4,500 and AED 5,500, each stepping up the stations, courses and staff. A private tasting ahead of a flagship launch is AED 1,400. The honest answer on cost is that it depends on your numbers and ambition, so we quote every job itemised — see our prices and catering price guide . A more affordable launch is possible, and the way to get there is to cut the station count rather than the food quality — three things done properly beats six done thinly, and it costs less.
